## The defect

`handleProjectPurge`'s destroy path pre-deleted only `working_copies`, `provenance_maps`, and
`analytics_events`, then issued the keyed `delete from projects` assuming the cascade reaches the
whole tree. It does not: prod `pg_constraint` marks a dozen project-tree edges **NO ACTION**
(`confdeltype='a'`) — the same class `handleAccountHardDelete` was fixed for live on 2026-10-01
(JOURNEY.1 — it tripped `claims_draft_id_fkey` then too). Any project that ran a Review (claims/
findings/correspondence) is unpurgeable: the 10-30 armed job died on it silently; the 11-15
re-arm died on it loudly ×3; every hourly tick keeps re-arming and failing until this lands.

## The leaf set — migrations enumerated, prod `pg_constraint` verified verbatim (2026-11-15T2x:4xZ)

Non-cascade FKs where **both** endpoints sit inside the `projects` cascade tree — so the row must
be deleted (or the edge severed) before the parent dies, because Postgres queues the NO-ACTION
check at the parent row's delete and the referencing row's own cascade-delete sits deeper in the
same trigger queue:

| Child → parent (constraint) | Delete-path depth | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `claims.draft_id → drafts` (`claims_draft_id_fkey`) | child depth-2 via `correspondence_items`; parent depth-1 | **explicit delete** (the observed blocker) |
| `findings.draft_id → drafts` | same | explicit delete |
| `correspondence_items.draft_id → drafts` | both depth-1 | explicit delete (evidence + parity) |
| `revision_obligations.opened_on_draft_id → drafts` | both depth-1 | explicit delete |
| `revision_obligations.finding_id → findings` | RO depth-1, findings depth-2 | explicit delete (before findings) |
| `obligation_findings.finding_id → findings` | OF depth-2 via RO | explicit delete (before findings) |
| `dispositions.response_id → correspondence_items` | ci depth-1, disp depth-3 via findings | explicit delete |
| `gates.step_id → steps` | both depth-2 via runs | explicit delete |
| `working_copies.base_draft_id / reconciled_into → drafts` | wc outside the tree | explicit delete (existing) |
| `working_copies.live_doc_id → live_docs` | wc outside; live_docs depth-2 | explicit delete — **new: the old delete missed this third ref** |
| `provenance_maps.draft_version_id → artifact_versions` | maps outside; versions depth-2 | explicit delete (existing) |
| `drafts.base_draft_id → drafts` (self) | same row set | within-project dies in one statement; **cross-project refs severed** (`update … set base_draft_id = null` on surviving rows) |
| `runs.parent_run_id → runs` (self) | same row set | same — **severed** on surviving rows |
| `runs.agent_instance_id → agent_instances` | both depth-1 | cascade-internal — both die in the keyed delete (sibling-proven ordering; never observed blocking) |
| `drafts.promoted_version_id → artifact_versions` | drafts depth-1, versions depth-2 | cascade-internal — versions' delete queues the check after drafts' cascade entry (sibling-proven) |
| `decision_requests.obligation_id → revision_obligations` | `confdeltype='n'` **SET NULL** | no action needed |

Edges whose parent **survives** the purge (`runs.requested_by→"user"`, `runs.workspace_id→workspaces`)
are irrelevant — deleting referencing rows never violates NO ACTION. Non-FK soft refs
(`analytics_events.project_id`, `inbox_items.project_id`) carry no constraint but are orphaned by
the destroy — both are deleted as hygiene (inbox_items is new; see judgement calls).

Ordering implemented (mirrors `handleAccountHardDelete`, 239 live completions):
`working_copies` → `provenance_maps` → `analytics_events` → `inbox_items` → `gates` (→decisions
cascade) → `decision_requests` → `obligation_findings` → `revision_obligations` (→transitions
cascade) → `dispositions` → `findings` → `claims` (→claim_sources cascade) →
`correspondence_items` → **sever pass** (`drafts.base_draft_id`, `runs.parent_run_id` nulled on
SURVIVING rows only — `project_id is distinct from $1`; both columns nullable, the schema's
intended resolution) → keyed `delete from projects` (cascades drafts/live_docs/restore_points,
runs/steps/events/decisions, artifacts/versions, agent_instances, guidance, threads, figures,
decision/obligation remnants, timeline/ai_use rows) → object-key cleanup (unchanged).
`ProjectPurgeResult.severed` added for honest accounting of the sever pass.

## Judgement calls

1. **`inbox_items` + `analytics_events` are deleted as destroy-hygiene, not FK necessity** —
   `inbox_items.project_id` is a soft column (no FK); a project-scoped notification outliving its
   project is a dangling-reference wart, and the `analytics_events` precedent (already deleted
   without an FK) extends. Both count under `deleted` honestly.
2. **Sever, not fail, for cross-project self-FK refs** — `drafts.base_draft_id` /
   `runs.parent_run_id` are nullable; a surviving row pointing into the tree would otherwise
   wedge the purge forever (or force deleting a SURVIVOR's row). Nulling loses a lineage pointer
   on the survivor — disclosed in the result's `severed` map; the schema's NO ACTION is exactly
   the sever-or-keep choice and keeping the parent is the contract being purged.
   `drafts.promoted_version_id` is deliberately NOT severed: frozen drafts require it non-null
   (`check (state <> 'frozen' or promoted_version_id is not null)`) and a cross-project promote
   target is pathological — that case still fails loudly, same as before, rather than corrupting
   a surviving frozen draft.
3. **`runs.agent_instance_id` + `drafts.promoted_version_id` left to the cascade** — both
   endpoints die inside the one keyed delete (same-statement NO ACTION siblings resolve; the
   sibling handler's 239 completions prove the ordering class). Enumerated in the comment so the
   map is complete, not pre-deleted (nothing to delete them by except the cascade itself).
4. **`decision_requests` kept in the explicit list** — `project_id` is CASCADE so it would die
   anyway; deleting it first mirrors the sibling and makes the per-table evidence count honest
   (its `obligation_id` SET-NULL edge then never even fires).
5. **`working_copies` delete extended to `live_doc_id`** — the old predicate covered
   base_draft_id/reconciled_into only; a wc keyed on the project's live_doc alone would have
   blocked `live_docs` (NO ACTION). Deleting such rows is the schema-intended resolution (the
   row's whole meaning is a copy OF the dying doc/draft).
6. **Per-statement autocommits preserved** (260's recorded posture) — idempotent under retry;
   one-transaction tightening remains a separate reviewed change.
